description: Selected ten configurations: eight principal cases and two one-change D02 interventions.

competitors.label: Baja reference
competitors.intent: Unchanged reference hardware; the common point of comparison.

competitors.label: Tip hardware 85%
competitors.intent: Change centrifugal closing and its consistent inertia together; spring and geometry unchanged. Higher/lower working speed is a hypothesis, not a guaranteed performance gain.

competitors.label: Tip hardware 115%
competitors.intent: Change centrifugal closing and its consistent inertia together; spring and geometry unchanged. Higher/lower working speed is a hypothesis, not a guaranteed performance gain.

competitors.label: Helix 28 deg
competitors.intent: Change the same constant-angle helix, measured from the circumferential direction; torque sensitivity and reflected shift inertia both change. Radius and preload unchanged.

competitors.label: Light weights + load reserve
competitors.intent: Candidate: higher engine working speed plus stronger secondary load response.

competitors.label: Very-light-tip flat-limit probe
competitors.intent: Larger single-knob mass reduction: distinguish persistent under-shifting from merely late high-ratio arrival.

competitors.label: Premature-shift stress control
competitors.intent: Intentionally adverse hypothesis: early primary closing and weak secondary opposition may pull the engine down under load.

competitors.label: Late-engagement stress control
competitors.intent: Intentionally adverse hypothesis: weak centrifugal closing against high preload may delay engagement or maintain primary slip.

competitors.label: D02: restore reference tip mass
competitors.intent: One-change intervention on D02: restore tip mass and its consistent mass moments while retaining the 115% primary preload. Assess traction, launch and shifting; no improvement is imposed.

competitors.label: D02: restore reference primary preload
competitors.intent: One-change intervention on D02: retain 65% tips but restore reference primary spring compression. Distinguish a lower spring opposition from increasing centrifugal actuation.
